headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and write conflicts between Mentat and RD-Agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes files and shares state via filesystem, while RD-Agent also uses files/logs and broad API/browser-driven workflows. That creates a plausible default bridge where one agent can ingest the other's outputs as trusted content. No MCP or clipboard bridge is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory, injected instructions in files can flow from one to the other.
IF RD-Agent writes logs or artifacts that Mentat later reads as task input, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable automatic ingestion of peer-generated files.
Review file inputs before passing between agents.
Use read-only mounts for shared reference data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mentat touches source code and has broad network egress; RD-Agent touches financial reports, datasets, execution traces, and logs and also has broad egress plus multiple API backends. If they share a workspace, sensitive material can move from one agent's files into the other's outputs or upstream APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF the two agents share a filesystem, source code or research artifacts can be exposed across the pair.
IF either agent forwards file contents to its model backend or external APIs, sensitive data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate credentials and workspaces.
Restrict network egress for one agent during shared runs.
Redact sensitive files before handoff.
Keep logs outside shared directories.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mentat can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem. RD-Agent also has file access and multiple instances support, so concurrent writes to the same workspace can race and corrupt code or logs. Because both can mutate shared state without documented locking, the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF RD-Agent writes logs while Mentat rewrites files in the same tree, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Run agents in separate clones.
Serialize write access with a lock file.
Disable git writes for one agent.
Keep logs in a separate directory.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and RD-Agent's research workflow can consume files, logs, and generated artifacts. If RD-Agent treats Mentat's outputs as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream research or automation. The pair is not documented as a verified handoff, so I keep this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF RD-Agent ingests Mentat-generated diffs or summaries without validation, incorrect edits can propagate.
IF Mentat's proposed changes are used as inputs to RD-Agent's automated research steps, downstream outputs may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Require human review before handoff.
Validate diffs against tests or linting.
Pass only structured summaries, not raw patches.
Log source provenance for each artifact.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Mentat handles source code and model-provider API keys, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, datasets, execution traces, and logs and uses multiple third-party APIs. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. I cite both because the risk arises from combining their data classes and external services.
conditions: IF regulated data from RD-Agent is processed alongside Mentat's external model calls, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF either agent logs sensitive inputs to shared storage, retention policy mismatches can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
Disable unnecessary logging.
Separate API keys by agent.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for sensitive data.
